summary: Susanville sits at roughly 4,200 feet in the high desert of northeastern California, ringed by the southern Cascades and the western edge of the Great Basin — a setting that delivers 9.1 hours of daily sunshine on average yet keeps daytime highs near a surprisingly mild 61°F annually, with nights dipping to 39°F, making it one of the colder small cities in the state. The local economy revolves heavily around public-sector employment: the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation operates two state prisons here — High Desert State Prison and the California Correctional Center — which together have historically been the dominant employers in the area, anchoring the tax base and shaping nearly every economic conversation. That public-sector weight helps explain a median household income of about $57,600 paired with a median home value around $234,000 — a price-to-income ratio just above 4:1, strikingly affordable by California standards, though the tradeoff is geographic isolation, with Reno roughly 85 miles southeast and Sacramento about 180 miles southwest. The Eagle Lake area north of town and the Susan River corridor offer genuine outdoor access for walking, fishing, and hiking without a long drive. Susanville is, at its core, a remote government-employment town where California housing math finally pencils out — but only because the nearest mid-size city is across a mountain pass.
